title: International Politics, B.A. -- International Political Economy Option (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Pre-2025 curriculum, built from the archived 2024-25 bulletin's own Suggested Academic Plan ('International Political Economy Option: International Politics, B.A. at University Park Campus') and Program Requirements ('International Political Economy Option (30 credits)') tabs -- confirmed course-code-identical to both 2022-23 and 2023-24 (this year's own course lists carry the same code set; only cosmetic title-text changes across the three years: GEOG 444's title changed from 'African Resources and Development' to 'Resource Governance in Africa' starting 2023-24, and this year's own boilerplate is the first to rename 'Other Cultures' to 'World Cultures' -- neither change touches any course code, credit value, or semester placement). Superseded starting 2025-26 by the addition of the two Liberal Arts Seminars (LA 83 in Semester 1, LA 283 in Semester 2) -- see INTPOL-2025.json / INTPOL-2026.json -- which raised the degree's total from 123 to 126 credits (both eras keep General Education Quantification in Second-Year Fall, this file's Semester 3, and General Education Course x2 in Second-Year Spring, Semester 4 -- built and verified directly from this year's own raw <table class="sc_plangrid"> HTML rows and printed per-semester subtotals (16/16/16/15/15/15/15/15 = 123), not the ambiguous flattened two-column text, which misleadingly suggests a GQ shift between semesters that the real table does not have). Same as INTPOL-2026.json: 'PLSC 412 (or 481)' and 'PLSC 418 (or 442)' are modeled as two separate real 2-way pools (per this year's own Program Requirements course list, which already lists them exactly this way -- 'PLSC 412 ... or PLSC 481 ...' and 'PLSC 418 ... or PLSC 442 ...' as two distinct 'Additional Courses' lines), not the Suggested-Academic-Plan table's simplified shared 'PLSC 412, 418, 439, or 442' display. 'LA' is dropped from this year's departments list since neither LA 83 nor LA 283 existed yet in 2024-25. Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. 'BA Fields' (3 occurrences), 'Elective (WAC)', and 'Elective (OC)' are modeled as generic slots, matching the bulletin's own open-selection phrasing, same convention as INTPOL-2026.json. 'PLSC 400-level Course' (Supporting Courses, 4 occurrences) is real per this year's own page but restricted to '400-level political science courses in International Relations, Comparative Politics, or Theory/Methodology' specifically -- left as a generic slot for the same reason given in INTPOL-2026.json. 'HIST/GEOG Option' (Semester 3) enumerated using only the codes independently confirmed present in this repo's own hist_catalog.json/geog_catalog.json, same set used in INTPOL-2026.json (this year's own course list published the identical HIST/GEOG code set, just with a few different course titles). 'ECON Advanced Course' (2 occurrences) enumerated from this year's own Economics Selection list: ECON 333/433/434/443/444/451/471/472N (all already real, cataloged, prereq-free courses; IB 303 is also part of the bulletin's own combined 9-credit ECON/IB selection pool but, matching INTPOL-2026.json's own scope, is left out here too since it isn't modeled there either).
